question_text:
For a superconducting material at a temperature $T$ below the critical temperature $T{C}$, the critical field $H{C}(T)$ depends on temperature according to the relationship

$$
H{C}(T)=H{C}(0)\left(1-\frac{T^{2}}{T{C}^{2}}\right)
$$

where $H{C}(0)$ is the critical field at 0 K .
(a) Using the data in  table 18.7 , calculate the critical magnetic fields for lead at 2.5 and 5.0 K .
(b) To what temperature must lead be cooled in a magnetic field of $15,000 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$ for it to be superconductive?

Reference:
 table 18.7 
Critical Temperatures and Magnetic Fluxes for Selected Superconducting Materials
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline Material & Critical Temperature $\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{C}}$ (K) & Critical Magnetic Flux Density $B_C\left(\right.$ tesla) ${ }^a$ \\
\hline \multicolumn{3}{|c|}{Elements ${ }^{\text {b }}$} \\
\hline Tungsten & 0.02 & 0.0001 \\
\hline Titanium & 0.40 & 0.0056 \\
\hline Aluminum & 1.18 & 0.0105 \\
\hline Tin & 3.72 & 0.0305 \\
\hline Mercury ( $\alpha$ ) & 4.15 & 0.0411 \\
\hline Lead & 7.19 & 0.0803 \\
\hline \multicolumn{3}{|c|}{Compounds and Alloys ${ }^{\boldsymbol{b}}$} \\
\hline $\mathrm{Nb}-\mathrm{Ti}$ alloy & 10.2 & 12 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Nb}-\mathrm{Zr}$ alloy & 10.8 & 11 \\
\hline $\mathrm{PbMo}_6 \mathrm{~S}_8$ & 14.0 & 45 \\
\hline $\mathrm{V}_3 \mathrm{Ga}$ & 16.5 & 22 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Nb}_3 \mathrm{Sn}$ & 18.3 & 22 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Nb}_3 \mathrm{Al}$ & 18.9 & 32 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Nb}_3 \mathrm{Ge}$ & 23.0 & 30 \\
\hline \multicolumn{3}{|c|}{Ceramic Compounds} \\
\hline $\mathrm{YBa}_2 \mathrm{Cu}_3 \mathrm{O}_7$ & 92 & - \\
\hline $\mathrm{Bi}_2 \mathrm{Sr}_2 \mathrm{Ca}_2 \mathrm{Cu}_3 \mathrm{O}_{10}$ & 110 & - \\
\hline $\mathrm{Tl}_2 \mathrm{Ba}_2 \mathrm{Ca}_2 \mathrm{Cu}_3 \mathrm{O}_{10}$ & 125 & - \\

${ }^a$ The critical magnetic flux density $\left(\mu_0 H_C\right)$ for the elements was measured at 0 K . For alloys and compounds, the flux is taken as $\mu_0 H_{C 2}$ (in teslas), measured at 0 K .

Give your answer as a tuple (the critical magnetic field in (a), temperature in (b)).The units of each required answer are (A/m, A/m, K), respectively.
response:
## Solution

**Given data for lead (from Table 18.7):**
- $T_C = 7.19\ \text{K}$
- $B_C(0) = 0.0803\ \text{T}$

Since $B_C = \mu_0 H_C$, the critical field at 0 K is:

$$H_C(0) = \frac{B_C(0)}{\mu_0} = \frac{0.0803}{4\pi\times10^{-7}} \approx 63900.7\ \text{A/m}$$

### (a) Critical fields at 2.5 K and 5.0 K

Using $H_C(T)=H_C(0)\!\left(1-\dfrac{T^{2}}{T_{C}^{2}}\right)$:

- At $T=2.5\ \text{K}$: $H_C = 63900.7\left(1-\frac{2.5^2}{7.19^2}\right) \approx 56175\ \text{A/m}$
- At $T=5.0\ \text{K}$: $H_C = 63900.7\left(1-\frac{5.0^2}{7.19^2}\right) \approx 32999\ \text{A/m}$

### (b) Temperature for superconductivity in $H = 15000\ \text{A/m}$

Setting $H_C(T)=15000$ and solving for $T$:

$$T = T_C\sqrt{1-\frac{H}{H_C(0)}} = 7.19\sqrt{1-\frac{15000}{63900.7}} \approx 6.29\ \text{K}$$

$$\boxed{(56175,\ 32999,\ 6.29)}$$
